scope: The channel contract a reader installs: the config every documented client route copies to ~/.omp/agent/config.yml now turns the pinned client's startup update check off (issue #18). All three client routes were re-run from their own quickstart blocks at the candidate - the macOS route from an isolated HOME on this Mac, the RTX 5090 native Windows client route on the appliance host, and the RTX 4090 native route on its host - and each run ends by asking the installed client what it actually reads.
question: Does a reader who follows any documented route end up on a client that will not advertise an out-of-channel `omp update`, and does that config leave the route's fail-closed behaviour intact?
answer: Yes. `examples/manual-tunnel/fail-closed.yml` gains `startup: checkUpdate: false`; the pinned 18.0.9 client reads it only in nested form - a dotted `startup.checkUpdate:` key leaves the default true, measured with `omp config get`. After each route the installed client reports false on all three hosts, and every route still passes end to end including its fail-closed check.
hosts: Mac (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, isolated HOME - the owner's client state was never moved), the RTX 5090 appliance's Windows client half, and the RTX 4090 host

run_notes.rtx5090-macos-client: Three attempts. Attempt 1 failed at the tool turn because the RTX 5090 Windows client route was running concurrently against the same inference host and its fail-closed block stops the shared runtime through stop-ninfer.sh, removing the container mid-run - an operator scheduling error, not a route defect: routes that share an inference host must be serialised. Attempt 2 failed at fail-closed on the forward attempt 1 left behind (the runner defect above). Attempt 3, recorded here, passed 10/10 in an isolated HOME on the candidate's runner. The first two attempts' receipts were discarded when the scratch tree was recreated; their outcomes are recorded here as observations only.
run_notes.rtx5090-windows-client: Passed 5/5 on the first attempt; its clone step was substituted with the candidate commit and verified installable, as every pre-cut run is.
run_notes.rtx4090-native: Three attempts. Attempt 1 failed at acceptance; attempt 2 failed at the provider block, which correctly refused to overwrite the models/config attempt 1 had installed - route-installed state must be cleared between runs on one host, which is what the clean-host step does for a first install. Attempt 3, recorded here, passed 7/7 on the rerun path with the 18 GB artifact already present.

corrections_to_earlier_records.claimed: "RTX 5090 appliance: production container serving … health ok, port and restart policy unchanged."
corrections_to_earlier_records.observed: Production `ninfer-5090-v051p` was stopped at 2026-09-11T23:59:37Z by the appliance's route-window script (`window.sh`), which pins its restart policy to `no` for a route window, and was never restored: it stayed down through the whole v0.6.5 cut and publication, with the lane supervisor's hold still engaged (paused=True), until 2026-09-12. The claim had been read off `omp-ninfer-beta` on port 18089 - the route's own container - not off production on 18088.
corrections_to_earlier_records.consequence: No v0.6.5 measurement or acceptance step is affected: every v0.6.5 route ran against the route container, which is what those routes install and use. What was false is the statement that the owner's production lane had been restored.
corrections_to_earlier_records.fixed: Production was restored on 2026-09-12 - healthy on 18088 in 10 s, restart policy back to `unless-stopped` - and the supervisor hold released. v0.6.5's published receipts are immutable and keep the incorrect sentence; this receipt is the correction of record and the v0.6.6 notes carry it.
corrections_to_earlier_records.class: an incumbent-restored claim must be measured on the incumbent's own port and restart policy, never on whatever container answers the route's port
